actuation: cable-driven actuation via stepper motor pulling nylon cables
thermal actuation via Joule heating of conductive polylactic acid (c-PLA) joints
constitutive_assumptions: Linear elastic isotropic material assumptions in finite element analysis (FEA) for distinct joint states: rigid joint stiffness assigned as 1.5 GPa and soft joint stiffness assigned as 0.15 GPa
Placement of the TPU/c-PLA interface along the neutral axis during bending to minimize interfacial delamination stresses
Tunneling-percolation model and Poisson's effect assumed to explain the negative gauge factor of the conductive TPU nanocomposite under strain
control_variables: Test coupon geometry: DMA specimens (40 mm x 12 mm x 0.55 mm) and 3-point flexural coupons (1 mm c-PLA and 1 mm TPU thickness)
DMA testing frequency (1 Hz) and thermal ramp rate (5 °C/min)
Cyclic fatigue stroke speed (600 mm/min) and deflection amplitude (5 mm)
3D printing parameters: layer height (0.2 mm), nozzle temperatures (c-PLA: 200 °C, TPU: 235 °C, c-TPU: 230 °C, nichrome embedding: 240 °C), print speeds, and infill types
Robot arm lifting velocity (5 cm/s) and vertical lift height (10 cm)
Resistance wire composition (80% Ni, 20% Cr) and wire diameter (0.4 mm)
dependent_variables: Storage modulus of PLA and c-PLA across temperature
Interlaminar tensile and shear strength at the TPU-c-PLA interface
Flexural stiffness of the bilayer joint coupons
Cyclic fatigue life (cycles to failure under repeated flexure)
Joint heating rate, temperature rise, and cooling rate
Grip force under different actuation configurations
Tactile sensor electrical resistance change, sensitivity, and output stability
Compressive force required for soft structure deformation

evidence_relevant_to_topic.claim: Bilayer conductive PLA and TPU joints allow temperature-controlled variable stiffness via Joule heating, dropping flexural stiffness from ~5000 N/m at 25 °C to less than 1000 N/m at 65 °C.

Heating c-PLA joints above their glass transition temperature (~60–65 °C) reduces bending stresses and prevents fatigue failure, whereas repeated bending in the high-stiffness state leads to cracks at approximately 400 cycles.

Embedding nichrome wire directly into conductive PLA during 3D printing creates robust electrical interconnects that provide uniform Joule heating and reduce heating time to reach 70 °C from >40 s at 0.1 A to <5 s at 0.3 A.

Integrating a c-PLA variable stiffness backbone with a soft TPU structure improves grasping force by up to 720% compared to an all-TPU counterpart, reaching a maximum grip force of 16.37 ± 0.33 N and supporting payloads up to 1.5 kg.

Multimaterial FFF 3D printing enables monolithic fabrication of a soft gripper with embedded conductive TPU resistive sensors that exhibit negative piezoresistive gauge behavior for tactile force sensing and object discrimination.
Finite element analysis demonstrates that selectively softening joints reduces internal bending stresses while rigid joints provide load-bearing support and resist bending under cable tension.

experimental_setup: Modified E3D ToolChanger multinozzle fused filament fabrication (FFF) 3D printer equipped with an in-house wire embedding module (0.8 mm nozzle and silicone-lined extruder gears)
Universal testing machine (Shimadzu AGX plus 10 kN) for tensile (ASTM D638), 3-point flexure (ASTM D790), lap shear (ASTM D3163), and cyclic fatigue testing
Dynamic mechanical analyzer (TA Instruments Q800) operating in 3-point bending configuration from 40 °C to 90 °C at 1 Hz
Thermal constant analyzer (Linseis THB-100 with THB type D QSS sensor) and forced convection oven for thermal conductivity characterization
MicroCT scanner (Bruker SkyScan 1173 with 19 μm pixel resolution) for non-destructive inspection of embedded nichrome wire interfaces
Infrared thermal camera (InfraTec VarioCAM HD head 600 at 12 Hz, 1016 x 720 resolution) for recording spatial heating and cooling profiles
Two-finger soft gripper mounted to a 6-DOF robotic arm (SHARE@NTU) driven by stepper motors, an Arduino Uno, and a 4-channel MOSFET powered by a 24 V DC supply
Multichannel digital multimeter connected to printed c-TPU sensor arrays for real-time electrical resistance measurements during manipulation trials
future_work: Incorporating a closed-loop temperature feedback control circuit for precise joint temperature regulation and overheating prevention
Developing holistic multi-sensor feedback systems to monitor structural health and joint conditions
Implementing active cooling mechanisms such as advanced printed fin geometries, external forced-convection cooling fans, or embedded liquid cooling channels
Applying machine learning algorithms (such as artificial neural networks) to classify tactile sensor array outputs and identify manipulated objects
Further optimizing the gripper design for broader deployment across industrial automation applications
independent_variables: Electrical current supplied for Joule heating (0.1 A, 0.2 A, 0.3 A)
Joint heating configuration (actuating lower joints only, upper joints only, or both joints)
Cooling configuration (joint with cooling fins vs. joint without fins)
Infill density of the 3D-printed TPU soft structure (10%, 15%, 20%)
Printing raster/infill orientation of the c-TPU sensor (0°, 45°, 90°)
Object shape, size, stiffness, and mass (tape roll, pyramid, bolt/nut, hand splint, complex decorative item, 1.5 kg dumbbell, and standard geometric blocks/rods)
limitations_inferred: Cable-driven actuation introduces friction and mechanical wear along internal guide channels over prolonged cycling
Repeated thermal cycling above the glass transition temperature of c-PLA may cause matrix degradation or alter conductive filler percolation networks over extended operational lifespans
Thermal time constants for natural convective cooling introduce latency between consecutive stiffness changes, limiting cycle speed in rapid manipulation tasks
External lead wires and acquisition equipment were manually connected to the embedded pins and sensors, indicating that electrical interface assembly is not fully monolithic
limitations_stated_by_authors: The gripper lacks a closed-loop temperature feedback control circuit, creating a risk of joint damage from localized or general overheating if unmonitored
Cooling rates evaluated in still air are relatively slow for rapid industrial cycles unless augmented by active cooling techniques
Interlaminar tensile (~1.5 MPa) and shear (~2.0 MPa) strengths between TPU and c-PLA are lower than bulk material values, requiring strategic placement near the neutral axis during bending
Lower infill densities (10% and 15%) in TPU led to sagging/overhanging print defects and unpredictable sensor output signals or secondary peak artifacts
Object identification and actuation mode classification based on sensor array profiles remain a hypothesis requiring further experimental validation and machine learning implementation
main_results: Conductive PLA displays a glass transition temperature of ~60–65 °C, with storage modulus dropping by 81% at 70 °C compared to room temperature (pure PLA drops by 93%).
The printed TPU/c-PLA interface achieved an average tensile strength of ~1.5 MPa and shear strength of ~2.0 MPa.
Flexural stiffness of bilayer TPU/c-PLA coupons decreased from ~5000 N/m at 25 °C to less than 1000 N/m at 65 °C.
Cyclic flexural testing at room temperature resulted in joint fracture at ~400 cycles, while coupons cycled at 60 °C showed no failure due to thermal stress relaxation above Tg.
Direct nichrome wire embedding enabled uniform Joule heating, reducing the heating time to reach 70 °C from >40 s to <5 s as current increased from 0.1 A to 0.3 A (~105–120 J energy required).
Finned joint designs significantly accelerated heat dissipation via natural convection compared to unfinned joints.
The variable-stiffness c-PLA backbone improved grip force by up to 720% compared to an all-TPU gripper, attaining a maximum grip force of 16.37 ± 0.33 N and lifting payloads up to 1.5 kg.
A 45° printed raster pattern and 20% infill density provided the highest sensitivity and output predictability for the c-TPU resistive tactile sensor without secondary peak artifacts.
Embedded multi-sensor arrays produced distinct normalized resistance readout signatures across various gripping modes, enabling touch detection and object discrimination.
modeling_methods: Finite Element Analysis (FEA) using Ansys Workbench 2020 to evaluate gripper deformation modes and stress distributions under rigid (1.5 GPa) and soft (0.15 GPa) joint stiffness conditions
Tunneling-percolation theory and Poisson's ratio considerations to model the negative gauge factor piezoresistive response of the conductive TPU nanocomposite under strain
performance_metrics: Storage modulus (MPa/GPa) and percentage reduction across the glass transition temperature
Interfacial tensile strength (MPa) and interlaminar shear strength (MPa)
Heating duration to reach 70 °C (s) and energy consumption (J)
Cooling rate and temperature drop over time (°C/s)
Grip force (N) and percentage improvement in grip force over pure TPU
Sensor sensitivity, gauge factor, and normalized resistance change (ΔR/R0)
possible_gap_implications: Thermal response latency during cooling highlights a general performance bottleneck in Joule-heated shape memory polymer grippers, pointing toward the need for integrated microfluidic cooling channels in monolithic additive manufacturing.

The trade-off between softness and sensor predictability at lower infill densities suggests a gap in fabricating soft cellular metamaterials that retain tactile sensing fidelity without structural drooping.
The lack of closed-loop thermal regulation underscores an architectural gap in variable-stiffness soft actuators, motivating future research into co-embedded thermomechanical sensory feedback.
paper.research_objective: To design and fabricate a multimaterial smart soft gripper with variable joint stiffness and integrated tactile sensing via a single-process 3D printing and wire embedding technique, minimizing manual assembly while balancing compliance, rigidity, payload capacity, and sensory feedback.
paper.research_problem: Balancing shape compliance, structural rigidity, low weight, and sensor integration in soft robotic grippers, while overcoming the weak actuation forces, multi-step assembly, and interfacial failure risks typical of conventional soft and multimaterial actuators.
stiffness_mechanism: thermoplastic phase change / glass transition thermal softening via Joule heating of conductive polylactic acid (c-PLA)
paper.title: A 3D Printing-Enabled Artificially Innervated Smart Soft Gripper with Variable Joint Stiffness
